intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Sunrise Temple Complex Tour
experiences.description: Explore the magnificent 12th-century Khmer temple complex at sunrise, wandering through Angkor Wat, Bayon, and Ta Prohm. Hire a local tuk-tuk driver for a full-day guided circuit covering the most iconic temples and learning about the ancient Khmer Empire's history and spiritual traditions.

experiences.name: Phnom Penh Historical & Cultural Immersion
experiences.description: Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda to admire Khmer architecture and sacred Buddhist artifacts, then pay respects at the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum and Choeung Ek Memorial to understand Cambodia's complex modern history. Round off the day exploring the vibrant riverside promenade and local markets.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Samloem Beach & Snorkeling Day
experiences.description: Take a ferry to the pristine island of Koh Rong Samloem and spend the day relaxing on the powder-white sands of Saracen Bay. Snorkel the crystal-clear turquoise waters teeming with tropical fish and coral, and enjoy fresh seafood at a beachside shack for an authentic Cambodian island experience.
experiences.location: Saracen Bay, Koh Rong Samloem, Sihanoukville

experiences.name: Siem Reap Khmer Cooking Class & Market Tour
experiences.description: Join a hands-on Khmer cooking class beginning with a guided tour of the Phsar Leu local market to select fresh ingredients like lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime. Learn to prepare traditional dishes such as Fish Amok, Lok Lak, and mango salad, gaining deep insight into Cambodian culinary culture and food traditions.
experiences.location: Old Market Area (Phsar Chas), Siem Reap

experiences.name: Kampot River Kayaking & Pepper Farm Visit
experiences.description: Kayak along the scenic Kampot River through lush mangroves and past French colonial architecture, then visit a renowned Kampot pepper farm to learn about the cultivation of one of the world's most prized spices. End the evening at a riverside restaurant sampling local crab dishes seasoned with fresh Kampot pepper.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take a tuk-tuk (~$5–7) to your boutique stay in the Angkor Archaeological Park area. Check in, freshen up, and take a slow walk around the immediate neighborhood to get your bearings. Visit the nearby Angkor Night Market entrance area to scope it out for later.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the famous Pub Street and Old Market (Psar Chaa) area in central Siem Reap (~15-minute tuk-tuk ride). Browse local stalls, pick up a SIM card if needed, and soak in the lively atmosphere of your first night in Cambodia.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport on arrival
meals.lunch: Quick bite at the airport or a local noodle shop near your hotel (~$2–3)
meals.dinner: Khmer Kitchen Restaurant on Pub Street — affordable authentic Khmer dishes like amok fish curry and lok lak for ~$3–5 per dish

day_by_day.notes: Exchange a small amount of USD or use an ATM at the airport. Cambodia widely accepts USD. Agree on tuk-tuk fares before riding. Rest early to prepare for full temple days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before sunrise (4:30 AM) for the iconic Angkor Wat sunrise experience. Purchase your Angkor Archaeological Park pass the evening before or at the gate (~$37 for a 1-day pass or $62 for a 3-day pass — highly recommend the 3-day pass). Watch the sunrise reflected in the lotus pond in front of Angkor Wat, then explore the temple's galleries, bas-reliefs, and central towers.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Angkor Wat, walk or tuk-tuk to Angkor Thom complex. Explore the South Gate with its massive stone faces, the Bayon Temple (famous for its 216 serene stone faces), the Baphuon, and the Elephant Terrace. Take a shaded rest during the hottest part of the day (12:00–14:00).
day_by_day.evening: Visit Ta Prohm — the atmospheric jungle temple where tree roots engulf ancient stone walls, famously used in the Tomb Raider film. The late afternoon golden light makes it magical. Return to town for dinner and a traditional Apsara dance performance.

meals.breakfast: Grab a baguette and coffee from a street vendor near the temple gate (~$1–2) — a French colonial legacy still popular in Cambodia
meals.lunch: Local rice and curry at a food stall near Angkor Thom (~$2–3)
meals.dinner: Marum Restaurant (training restaurant supporting at-risk youth) — delicious Khmer tapas for ~$4–7 per dish; worth every cent

day_by_day.notes: Bring at least 2 liters of water, sunscreen, a hat, and comfortable walking shoes. Temples open at 5:00 AM. Dress modestly — shoulders and knees must be covered. A tuk-tuk driver hired for the day costs ~$15–20 and is well worth it.

day_by_day.morning: Use your 3-day Angkor pass for the outer temple circuit. Start early at Preah Khan — a sprawling jungle temple with long corridors, moss-covered stones, and a serene atmosphere with far fewer crowds than Angkor Wat. Then visit Neak Pean, a small but unique island temple built on an artificial pond.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Ta Som, a compact but beautiful overgrown temple, and then East Mebon, a temple pyramid originally surrounded by a large reservoir. Finish with Pre Rup, a 10th-century temple mountain offering panoramic views — perfect for late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap and visit the Angkor Night Market for souvenir shopping. Handmade scarves, silverware, and paintings make great budget gifts. Practice your bargaining skills respectfully.

meals.breakfast: Banana pancake and fresh fruit smoothie from a guesthouse café near your hotel (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snacks from a local market near the temples (~$2)
meals.dinner: Khmer BBQ (Cambodian-style grilled meats and vegetables cooked at your table) at a local restaurant near Pub Street (~$5–8 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The outer circuit temples are less crowded and more atmospheric — arrive early for the best experience. Carry snacks as food stalls near outer temples are limited. November weather in Cambodia is generally pleasant and dry — ideal for temple exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Use your 3-day Angkor pass for the final day. Head to Banteay Srei (~30 km north of Siem Reap, ~45-min tuk-tuk ride), known as the 'Citadel of Women' — its intricate pink sandstone carvings are considered the finest in all of Angkor. Arrive early before tour buses. Nearby, visit Banteay Samré, a lesser-visited but beautifully preserved Hindu temple.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the Landmine Museum on the way back — a sobering but important cultural and historical experience explaining Cambodia's tragic history with landmines, run by a former child soldier turned activist. Admission ~$5. Then visit the Cambodia Cultural Village near Siem Reap for a condensed overview of Cambodia's diverse ethnic groups and traditions.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset cocktail (or fresh coconut) at one of the rooftop bars on Pub Street. Then explore the lively night food market for street snacks.

meals.breakfast: Rice porridge (bobor) with egg and ginger at a local Khmer breakfast spot (~$1.50–2)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Banteay Srei — try a Khmer noodle soup (kuy teav) (~$2–3)
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at the Night Market food court — grilled corn, spring rolls, fried noodles (~$3–5 total)

day_by_day.notes: Hire a tuk-tuk for the full day for the Banteay Srei trip (~$20–25 including waiting time). The Landmine Museum is deeply moving — visit with respect. This is your last day on the Angkor pass, so make it count.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning boat trip on Tonle Sap Lake — the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Visit a floating village (Kampong Phluk or Kompong Khleang) to see how communities live on water. Boat tours depart from Chong Kneas (~$10–15 for a shared boat tour).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siem Reap and visit the Angkor National Museum (~$12 entry) for a deep-dive into Khmer history, art, and the story of Angkor. Well air-conditioned — a perfect afternoon activity. Afterward, take a free walking tour of the French Quarter of Siem Reap to see colonial architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost traditional Apsara dance performance. Several restaurants offer free shows with dinner — Koulen Restaurant and Angkor Village Resort are popular options. Book ahead.

meals.breakfast: French baguette with pâté or egg from a street bakery (~$1–2)
meals.lunch: Floating village restaurant on the lake — fresh fish dishes (~$3–5)
meals.dinner: Set dinner menu with Apsara dance show at Koulen Restaurant (~$10–12 including show)

day_by_day.notes: The floating village tours can be touristy — opt for Kompong Khleang for a more authentic experience (further away, ~$25–30 for a private tuk-tuk). Respect local residents and avoid intrusive photography. Today is a slower-paced day — enjoy it.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a budget bus from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (Cambodia's capital). Giant Ibis or Mekong Express buses depart at ~7:00–8:00 AM and cost ~$10–15 for a comfortable 6-hour journey. Book online in advance. Enjoy the countryside views along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh (~13:00–14:00). Check into a budget guesthouse in the BKK1 or Riverside area (~$10–20/night for a clean private room). Drop bags and head to the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda (~$10 entry) — a stunning complex of gilded spires, sacred Buddha statues, and manicured gardens along the Mekong riverfront.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Sisowath Quay (Phnom Penh Riverside promenade) as the sun sets over the Mekong and Tonle Sap confluence. Browse street food vendors and watch locals gather for evening exercise and socializing.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at your Siem Reap hotel or a café near the bus station before departure (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Snacks and packed food on the bus, or stop at a roadside restaurant during the journey (~$2–4)
meals.dinner: Riverside restaurant on Sisowath Quay — try amok fish curry or beef lok lak with river views (~$4–7)

day_by_day.notes: Book your bus ticket at least a day in advance, especially on weekends. Giant Ibis is highly recommended for safety and reliability. Store valuables securely on the bus. Phnom Penh is a bigger, busier city — be more vigilant with belongings.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school turned Khmer Rouge prison where thousands were tortured. One of the most important and sobering historical sites in Southeast Asia (~$8 entry). Allow at least 2 hours. An audio guide is available for ~$3 and is strongly recommended.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk (~$10–15 return) to the Choeung Ek Killing Fields (~15 km from the city center) — a deeply emotional memorial site with a Buddhist stupa filled with skulls and bones of victims. The audio tour (~$6) is exceptional and tells individual stories of survivors and victims. Allow 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city and decompress with a quiet walk through the Central Market (Psar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco dome market selling jewelry, clothing, and souvenirs. Then enjoy dinner at a local restaurant with something comforting.

meals.breakfast: Congee (rice porridge) with fried dough sticks from a local market stall (~$1.50)
meals.lunch: Simple Khmer rice dish at a local canteen near Tuol Sleng (~$2–3)
meals.dinner: Friends the Restaurant (social enterprise supporting street youth) — creative Khmer-fusion tapas for ~$4–8 per dish

day_by_day.notes: Today is emotionally heavy but historically essential. Dress respectfully (covered shoulders and knees). Take your time and allow space for reflection. The Killing Fields and S-21 together form one of the most important historical experiences in Cambodia — do not rush. Consider journaling in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day to Sihanoukville (for beach access). Take the morning Giant Ibis or Mekong Express bus from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville (~4.5–5 hours, ~$10–12). Alternatively, take a direct bus to Kampot (~3 hours, ~$8) for a more relaxed coastal town experience — recommended for budget travelers seeking a quieter beach vibe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Kampot (~12:30–13:00). Check into a budget riverside guesthouse (~$10–18/night). Rent a bicycle (~$2–3/day) and explore the charming French colonial town center, pepper plantations on the outskirts, and the relaxed riverside promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat cruise on the Kampot River — many guesthouses and tour operators offer shared sunset cruises for ~$5–8 per person, often including a drink. Watch fireflies emerge after dark along the mangrove-lined riverbanks.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Phnom Penh guesthouse or a café before the bus (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Snack on the bus or grab food at the Kampot bus drop-off (~$2)
meals.dinner: Rusty Keyhole or Epic Arts Café in Kampot — relaxed riverside dining with Khmer and Western options (~$4–7 per dish)

day_by_day.notes: Kampot is a far more relaxed and budget-friendly alternative to the increasingly overdeveloped Sihanoukville. It offers a charming mix of colonial architecture, pepper farms, river life, and proximity to Kep beach. Highly recommended for travelers seeking culture AND beaches on a budget.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a motorbike (~$8–10/day, or join a guided tour for ~$15) and ride to Bokor National Park — a hauntingly beautiful abandoned French hill station at 1,000m elevation with a ruined casino, old church, and sweeping views over the Gulf of Thailand. The ride up is dramatic and the cooler air is refreshing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from Bokor and take a short tuk-tuk or shared taxi to Kep (~30 minutes, ~$5–8). Kep is a tiny, peaceful seaside town famous for its crab market. Walk along the beach, swim in the warm Gulf of Thailand waters, and browse the famous Kep Crab Market.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for sunset at the Kep Crab Market — watch fishermen bring in their catch as the sky turns orange. Then return to Kampot for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Khmer breakfast of rice and egg soup at a local market stall in Kampot (~$1.50–2)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or a quick bite at a roadside stall near Bokor (~$2)
meals.dinner: Fresh pepper crab at the Kep Crab Market — a must-try Cambodian delicacy! (~$6–10 for a generous serving) or back in Kampot at a riverside restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Bokor National Park requires an entrance fee (~$5). If renting a motorbike, ensure you are comfortable riding on mountain roads. Alternatively, hire a tuk-tuk driver for the full day (~$20–25). Kep's beach is small but charming — Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay) nearby offers better swimming if time allows (~$5 boat ride).

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a final sunrise walk along the Kampot riverside. Visit the Kampot Pepper Farm for a free or low-cost tour (~$2–5) — Kampot pepper is world-renowned and makes an excellent, lightweight souvenir. Learn about the cultivation process and taste different varieties.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back toward Phnom Penh or Sihanoukville airport depending on your departure flight. Take a shared taxi or bus from Kampot (~$7–10 to Phnom Penh, 3 hours). If time allows before departure, do a final browse of the Russian Market (Psar Tuol Tom Poung) in Phnom Penh for last-minute souvenirs — silk scarves, spices, and handicrafts at good prices.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Phnom Penh or at the airport. Reflect on 10 incredible days of temples, history, culture, and beaches across Cambodia.

meals.breakfast: Final Cambodian breakfast — fried rice with egg and fresh lime juice at a local market (~$2)
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant on the way back to Phnom Penh (~$3–4)
meals.dinner: A farewell Cambodian meal — fish amok, green mango salad, and sticky rice with mango for dessert at a local Khmer restaurant (~$5–8)

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate for 10 days: Accommodation ~$100–180, Food ~$80–120, Transport ~$60–90, Entrance fees ~$80–100, Activities ~$40–60. Total estimated budget: ~$360–550 USD for 10 days — very achievable for a budget-conscious traveler. Book return transport in advance. Cambodia visa on arrival is available for most nationalities (~$30 USD). Always carry small USD bills.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and transit time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your boutique stay near Angkor Archaeological Park. Freshen up, then take a relaxed tuk-tuk ride through the Angkor complex entrance roads to get oriented. Visit the nearby Angkor Conservation Office area and stroll the grounds around your hotel to acclimatize.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Pub Street and the Old Market (Psar Chas) area in Siem Reap town for a lively introduction to the city. Browse local craft stalls and soak up the atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a nearby café after check-in — try a bowl of Khmer noodle soup (kuy teav) at a local eatery near the hotel for around $3–5.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mahob Restaurant or Cuisine Wat Damnak area — enjoy authentic Khmer set menu with amok fish and lok lak beef. Budget $12–18 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 3-day or 7-day Angkor Pass at the official ticket office (open until 17:30) on your way from the airport — saves time tomorrow morning. Tuk-tuk from airport costs roughly $8–10.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early (5:30 AM) for sunrise at Angkor Wat — one of the world's most iconic sunrises reflected in the main pond. Explore the outer galleries and bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk and the Mahabharata scenes. Hire a knowledgeable local guide ($20–25) for deeper historical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue inside Angkor Wat to the upper levels and central sanctuary. After lunch, visit Angkor Thom complex — enter through the South Gate with its 54 stone faces, explore the Bayon Temple with its 216 enigmatic stone faces, and walk through the Baphuon and Terrace of the Elephants.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap town. Enjoy a traditional Apsara dance performance at Angkor Village Theatre or Smile of Angkor ($15–25 per person including dinner show option).

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at your hotel or a grab-and-go baguette from a street vendor near the park entrance ($1–2).
meals.lunch: Blue Pumpkin or a local restaurant near Angkor Thom — try Khmer red curry with rice. Budget $6–10.
meals.dinner: Dinner included in Apsara show package, or dine at Haven Restaurant (social enterprise training restaurant) — excellent Khmer cuisine at $10–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: November weather is ideal — dry season begins, temperatures around 28–32°C. Wear light clothing, bring sunscreen and a hat. Start no later than 5:15 AM for the best sunrise spot.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the jungle-clad Ta Prohm temple — famously left partially unrestored with massive tree roots engulfing the stone walls (known as the 'Tomb Raider temple'). A deeply atmospheric and photogenic site. Then visit Banteay Kdei and the serene Srah Srang reservoir.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Pre Rup temple for panoramic views over the jungle canopy, then visit East Mebon. Alternatively, visit the Angkor National Museum in Siem Reap town ($12 entry) for a comprehensive overview of Khmer civilization, art, and the history of the Angkor Empire.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Artisans Angkor workshop (free entry, closes 18:30) to watch craftspeople practice traditional Khmer silk weaving, stone carving, and lacquerware. Browse and shop for quality souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or Café Central near Pub Street — eggs, fresh fruit, coffee. $4–7.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from a local market near Ta Prohm or eat at a roadside Khmer stall — rice with grilled chicken and vegetables. $3–5.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malis Restaurant — upscale Khmer cuisine in a beautiful garden setting. Try the tasting menu. $15–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Ta Prohm gets crowded mid-morning; arrive by 8:00 AM for a quieter experience. The Angkor National Museum is air-conditioned — a good afternoon refuge from the heat.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Banteay Srei — the 'Citadel of Women,' a 10th-century temple renowned for its intricate pink sandstone carvings, considered the finest decorative work in all of Angkor. Located 25 km north of Siem Reap (45-min tuk-tuk ride). Arrive early before tour buses.
day_by_day.afternoon: On the return journey, stop at the Landmine Museum (free/donation) — a sobering and important cultural site documenting Cambodia's tragic history with landmines and the ongoing demining efforts. Then visit Banteay Samré, a less-visited but beautifully preserved temple.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Siem Reap, enjoy a sunset cocktail at Miss Wong cocktail bar (colonial-era Shanghai speakeasy vibe) or rooftop bar at Rosewood or Park Hyatt. Then explore the Night Market along the river.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at your hotel before the early departure.
meals.lunch: Eat at a local restaurant in the Banteay Srei village area — fresh spring rolls and grilled fish. $4–7.
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at the Siem Reap Night Market food court — try nom banh chok (Khmer noodles), grilled corn, and fresh coconut. $5–8 for a full spread.

day_by_day.notes: Hire a tuk-tuk for the full day to Banteay Srei — negotiate around $20–25 for the full-day circuit. The Landmine Museum is deeply moving; not recommended for very young children.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Phnom Bakheng — a hilltop temple with panoramic views over the Angkor plain and Tonlé Sap Lake in the distance. Then explore the lesser-visited but impressive Preah Khan temple — a vast jungle temple with long colonnaded corridors and a serene atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a boat trip on Tonlé Sap Lake — Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake. Visit a floating village (Chong Kneas or Kampong Phluk) to witness the unique way of life of communities living entirely on water, including floating schools, churches, and restaurants.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset over Tonlé Sap Lake from the boat is spectacular. Return to Siem Reap and enjoy a relaxing evening with a traditional Khmer massage ($8–12/hour) at one of many reputable spas near your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel.
meals.lunch: Fresh fish lunch at a floating restaurant on Tonlé Sap Lake — grilled catfish with rice and vegetables. $7–12.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Viroth's Restaurant — elegant Khmer fine dining in a beautiful garden. Try the amok and the banana blossom salad. $15–20 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Tonlé Sap boat tours cost approximately $15–20 per person. November is a great time to visit — the lake is at its largest after the rainy season. Kampong Phluk is more scenic but requires a longer boat ride.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a bus or private taxi from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (approximately 5–6 hours by bus, $10–15, or 4 hours by private taxi, $60–80). Book a reputable bus company like Giant Ibis or Mekong Express for comfort and reliability.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh early afternoon. Check in to your mid-range hotel (Pavilion or similar boutique guesthouse in BKK1 area, $40–70/night). Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — a stunning complex of Khmer royal architecture with gilded spires, housing the Emerald Buddha and a floor of 5,000 silver tiles.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Sisowath Quay riverside promenade as the sun sets over the Tonlé Sap and Mekong confluence. Enjoy the lively atmosphere with locals and travelers alike.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch on the bus or at a rest stop along National Road 6 — local rice dishes available at roadside restaurants. $3–5.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Friends Restaurant (Mith Samlanh) — a beloved social enterprise training restaurant. Excellent tapas-style Khmer and fusion dishes. $10–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book your bus ticket at least a day in advance, especially on weekends. Giant Ibis is highly recommended for safety and punctuality. Store valuables securely during the journey.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school turned Khmer Rouge prison and now a haunting memorial to the approximately 17,000 people who were imprisoned and tortured there between 1975–1979. An essential, sobering, and deeply important historical experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (The Killing Fields), located 15 km south of the city. The audio guide ($6) is exceptionally moving and informative. A stupa filled with victims' skulls serves as a memorial. Afterward, visit the National Museum of Cambodia — stunning terracotta pavilion housing the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture and artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Take time to process the day's heavy history with a quiet riverside walk. Visit the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco yellow dome market — for evening browsing and light shopping.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local bakery near your hotel — French-influenced Cambodian breakfast of baguette, pâté, and café sua (iced coffee with condensed milk). $3–5.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near Tuol Sleng — Java Café or similar. $6–10.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Romdeng Restaurant (sister to Friends) — specializing in Cambodian countryside cuisine including deep-fried tarantulas for the adventurous. $12–18 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek are emotionally intense. Take breaks as needed and be respectful. Not recommended for children under 12. Hiring a tuk-tuk for the full day in Phnom Penh costs about $15–20.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a bus or shared taxi from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville (approximately 4 hours, $10–12 by bus). From Sihanoukville port, take a fast ferry to Koh Rong Sanloem island (45–60 minutes, $25–35 round trip). Check in to a mid-range beachfront bungalow ($40–70/night).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Koh Rong Sanloem — one of Cambodia's most beautiful islands with pristine white sand beaches and crystal-clear turquoise water. Settle in, then spend the afternoon relaxing on Saracen Bay or the quieter M'Pai Bay. Swim, snorkel, or simply unwind.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the beach with a cold Angkor beer. After dark, experience the magical bioluminescent plankton — wade into the shallow water at night to see the blue glowing light. Best experienced away from bright lights on quieter stretches of beach.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel before early departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch on the ferry or at a beachside shack upon arrival — fresh grilled fish, rice, and mango shake. $5–8.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beachfront restaurant on Saracen Bay — grilled whole snapper, coconut curry, and fresh fruit. $10–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets in advance during peak season. November is excellent for the islands — calm seas, warm water, and clear skies. Bring cash as ATMs are limited on the island. Sunscreen is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Join a half-day snorkeling trip around Koh Rong Sanloem's coral reefs — organized through your guesthouse or local operators ($15–20 per person). See colorful reef fish, sea turtles, and vibrant coral gardens. Visit the secluded Lazy Beach on the western side of the island (accessible by boat or jungle trek).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the island on foot — hike through the jungle interior trail connecting Saracen Bay to M'Pai Bay (approximately 45-minute walk through tropical forest). Visit the small fishing village at M'Pai Bay for an authentic glimpse of island life. Kayak rental available at most guesthouses ($5–8/hour).
day_by_day.evening: Final island evening — enjoy a bonfire beach barbecue if available at your resort, or dine at a beachfront restaurant with your feet in the sand. Star-gazing from the beach is exceptional due to minimal light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Tropical breakfast at your bungalow — fresh papaya, pineapple, eggs, and strong Cambodian coffee. $4–7.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the snorkeling boat or beachside at Lazy Beach — sandwiches, fruit, and drinks. $5–8.
meals.dinner: Beachfront BBQ dinner — grilled prawns, squid, and fish with local sauces and sticky rice. $12–18 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Respect the marine environment — do not touch coral or feed fish. Bring biodegradable sunscreen to protect the reef. The jungle trail to M'Pai Bay can be muddy — wear sturdy sandals or light hiking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on Koh Rong Sanloem — one last swim and walk along the beach at sunrise. Pack up and take the morning ferry back to Sihanoukville. Depending on your departure flight, either head directly to Phnom Penh International Airport (4 hours) or Siem Reap (6+ hours) via arranged private transfer or bus.
day_by_day.afternoon: If time allows before your onward journey, stop in Sihanoukville for lunch and a quick browse of the local market. Alternatively, relax at an airport hotel or lounge if your flight departs from Phnom Penh in the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on an extraordinary 10 days — from the ancient temples of Angkor and the historical weight of Phnom Penh to the paradise beaches of Koh Rong Sanloem. Cambodia's rich history, warm culture, and natural beauty make it a truly unforgettable destination.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at your island bungalow before ferry departure — toast, fruit, and coffee. $3–5.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Sihanoukville — try a local Khmer restaurant near the port for a final bowl of fish amok or beef lok lak. $5–10.
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight dining depending on departure time. If time permits, grab Cambodian street food snacks for the journey — nom pang (Cambodian baguette sandwich) for $1–2.

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry and bus schedules the evening before to plan your departure timing carefully. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for travel to the airport. Consider booking a private transfer for the final day to reduce stress. Keep some US dollars and Cambodian Riel for final tips and small purchases — tipping is appreciated but not mandatory.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to your boutique stay within Angkor Archaeological Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private welcome orientation and check-in at your boutique property. After freshening up, enjoy a leisurely guided walk through the immediate temple grounds near your accommodation — a gentle introduction to the Angkor complex with a personal historian guide. Visit the nearby Baksei Chamkrong temple, a smaller, intimate 10th-century pyramid temple perfect for an unhurried first encounter with Khmer architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on your hotel's terrace or rooftop overlooking the jungle canopy. Followed by a private welcome dinner at your resort's signature restaurant featuring refined Khmer cuisine — amok trey (fish amok in banana leaf), lok lak beef, and fresh tropical fruit desserts paired with curated Cambodian wines.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread at the hotel upon arrival — fresh coconut water, seasonal tropical fruits, Cambodian spring rolls, and cold brew iced tea
meals.dinner: Private welcome dinner at the boutique resort's signature restaurant — traditional Khmer tasting menu with sommelier-selected wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Arrive rested and hydrated. November is the beginning of Cambodia's cool dry season — expect pleasant temperatures around 27–30°C. Light linen clothing recommended. Ensure jet lag is managed; keep Day 1 relaxed to prepare for early temple visits ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn private transfer to Angkor Wat for an exclusive sunrise viewing — one of the world's most iconic spectacles. Arrive by 05:15 to secure a prime reflecting pool position. A private expert guide narrates the temple's 12th-century Khmer history, Vishnu mythology, and the extraordinary bas-relief galleries stretching over 800 meters. Explore the inner sanctum at leisure before the crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom — the great walled royal city. Visit the Bayon Temple with its 216 enigmatic stone faces, the Baphuon pyramid temple, the Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Enjoy a private air-conditioned tuk-tuk or vintage Jeep tour between sites. Midday retreat to the hotel for a rest and a refreshing pool dip during peak heat hours.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive Apsara dance performance dinner — a private or semi-private setting at a heritage venue in Siem Reap featuring traditional Khmer classical dance, UNESCO-recognized as intangible cultural heritage. Multi-course royal Khmer banquet served during the performance.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast hamper served at Angkor Wat's reflecting pool at sunrise — croissants, fresh fruit, Cambodian rice porridge (bobor), fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Elegant garden lunch at Malis Restaurant or equivalent fine-dining Khmer establishment in Siem Reap — green mango salad, grilled fish with lemongrass, and palm sugar crème brûlée
meals.dinner: Royal Khmer banquet at a heritage Apsara performance venue — amok, lok lak, banana blossom salad, jasmine rice, and tropical dessert platter

day_by_day.notes: Set alarm for 04:30. Bring insect repellent and a light layer for the pre-dawn chill. Photography golden hour at sunrise is extraordinary — a professional photography guide can be arranged on request.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided exploration of Ta Prohm — the legendary jungle temple famously left intertwined with massive silk-cotton and strangler fig trees. Visit early morning for atmospheric lighting and fewer visitors. Your guide contextualizes the temple's original function as a Buddhist monastery and its 19th-century 'rediscovery.' Proceed to Preah Khan, another sprawling jungle complex with long colonnaded corridors and intricate carvings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Angkor National Museum in Siem Reap for a deep-dive cultural context session — eight galleries covering Khmer civilization, the Hindu-Buddhist cosmology embedded in temple design, and the great kings of Angkor. Followed by a private batik or silk weaving workshop at a local artisan cooperative — try your hand at traditional Cambodian textile arts and select premium silk scarves as souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a luxury rooftop restaurant in Siem Reap's heritage quarter — contemporary Cambodian cuisine with French-colonial influences. Stroll through the Pub Street and Old Market (Phsar Chas) area for atmospheric evening exploration and artisan shopping.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at the hotel — Cambodian congee with accompaniments, eggs Benedict, tropical fruit platter, freshly baked pastries, and specialty Cambodian coffee (Kampot robusta)
meals.lunch: Refined lunch at Cuisine Wat Damnak or equivalent — seasonal tasting menu using local Cambodian ingredients with creative modern presentation
meals.dinner: Rooftop fine dining at a Siem Reap heritage restaurant — Cambodian-French fusion tasting menu with wine flight

day_by_day.notes: Comfortable walking shoes essential for temple exploration. Ta Prohm can be slippery — watch your step on moss-covered stones. The silk weaving workshop supports local artisan communities and makes for a meaningful cultural experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip to Banteay Srei — the 'Citadel of Women,' a 10th-century temple renowned for its extraordinarily intricate pink sandstone carvings, considered the finest examples of Khmer decorative art. Located 25 km north of Angkor, this gem is best appreciated with a specialist art historian guide who can decode the mythological narratives in the carvings.
day_by_day.afternoon: En route back, stop at Banteay Samré — a lesser-visited but beautifully preserved 12th-century temple surrounded by a moat. Enjoy the tranquility and exclusivity of having the site nearly to yourself. Return to the hotel for a luxury spa afternoon — traditional Khmer massage, herbal compress treatment, and a floral bath ritual at the resort's wellness center.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset boat cruise on Tonlé Sap Lake — Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake, a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Witness the floating villages, observe local fishing communities, and enjoy champagne and canapés as the sun sets over the vast water expanse. Return to the hotel for a relaxed private dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fresh tropical smoothie bowls, Cambodian banana pancakes, eggs to order, artisan bread, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the hotel chef — served in the shade of Banteay Srei's outer courtyard with linen service, cold-pressed juices, and Cambodian finger foods
meals.dinner: Private in-room or terrace dinner at the boutique resort — chef's tasting menu with personalized Khmer and international selections

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is a must for art and history lovers — allocate at least 2 hours. The spa session should be pre-booked. Tonlé Sap Lake cruise timings depend on seasonal water levels; November is ideal as the lake is at maximum size after the monsoon retreat.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Remote Roluos Group — the oldest surviving major temples near Angkor, dating to the 9th century. Visit Preah Ko, Bakong (the first temple-mountain of the Khmer Empire), and Lolei. These rarely visited sites offer a profound sense of historical depth and near-solitary exploration with your private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private cooking class with a celebrated Cambodian chef — visit the local Siem Reap market to select fresh ingredients (Kampot pepper, kaffir lime, galangal, palm sugar), then prepare three classic Khmer dishes in a luxury villa kitchen setting. Enjoy your creations for lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Phnom Penh via private charter flight (approximately 45-minute flight, far preferable to the 6-hour drive for a luxury itinerary). Check in at a 5-star Phnom Penh property — The Raffles Hotel Le Royal or equivalent. Evening at leisure — a nightcap at the legendary Elephant Bar at Raffles, a colonial-era institution.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Cambodian noodle soup (kuy teav), fresh fruit, pastries, and Cambodian iced coffee
meals.lunch: Your own Khmer cooking class creations — fish amok, beef lok lak, and green mango salad, served with jasmine rice and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Dinner at Raffles Le Royal's Restaurant Le Royal — classic French-Cambodian cuisine in a stunning 1929 colonial dining room

day_by_day.notes: Private charter flights between Siem Reap and Phnom Penh should be booked well in advance. Alternatively, a luxury private road transfer can be arranged for those preferring to see the countryside. Pack light for the flight — luggage transfer can be coordinated by the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda in Phnom Penh — the glittering centerpiece of the Cambodian capital. Explore the Throne Hall, the Napoleon III Pavilion, and the Silver Pagoda (Wat Preah Keo) with its floor of 5,000 silver tiles and priceless Emerald Buddha. Your guide provides royal court history and Theravada Buddhist context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sobering but essential cultural visit to the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) and the Choeung Ek Memorial (Killing Fields) — guided by a specialist historian. This is a profoundly important experience for understanding modern Cambodian history and the resilience of its people. Allow 3–4 hours with reflective breaks.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails aboard a private luxury river cruise along the Tonlé Sap and Mekong confluence — champagne and artisan canapés as the sun sets over the Phnom Penh skyline. Dinner at Malis Phnom Penh — one of Cambodia's finest restaurants, celebrating authentic Cambodian haute cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Raffles Le Royal breakfast — full buffet and à la carte options including Cambodian dim sum, tropical fruits, freshly baked breads, and specialty coffees
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a riverside café near the Royal Palace — fresh spring rolls, Cambodian iced tea, and coconut desserts
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malis Phnom Penh — signature tasting menu featuring Cambodian heirloom recipes with premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally intense — dress respectfully and allow time for reflection. These sites are critically important for cultural understanding and are handled with great sensitivity by specialist guides. Keep the evening's river cruise as a gentle, restorative transition.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Cambodia — Southeast Asia's largest archaeological museum, housing the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture and art. Private curator-led tour of the galleries, including the pre-Angkorian bronzes, Angkor-era sandstone masterpieces, and ethnographic collections. Followed by a walk through the charming riverside Sisowath Quay promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Kep — a 3-hour scenic drive through rural Cambodia to the sleepy French colonial seaside resort town on the Gulf of Thailand. Check in at a boutique luxury property in Kep — Song Saa Private Island (if arranging island extension) or a premium cliff-top villa overlooking the sea.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Kep's famous crab market — the town's legendary specialty. Private dinner at your accommodation or at a premium Kep seafood restaurant — freshly caught Kep crab stir-fried with Kampot pepper (the world's finest pepper, grown just 25 km away), grilled lobster, and steamed clams.

meals.breakfast: Raffles Le Royal breakfast — eggs Benedict, tropical fruit, Cambodian rice porridge, freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Roadside gourmet stop en route to Kep — curated lunch box prepared by the Raffles kitchen, enjoyed at a scenic rural rest stop or riverside location
meals.dinner: Premium seafood dinner in Kep — Kampot pepper crab, grilled whole snapper, lobster thermidor, with chilled Sancerre or Chablis

day_by_day.notes: The drive to Kep passes through Cambodian countryside — rice paddies, sugar palm trees, and rural village life. An excellent opportunity for photography. Arrive in Kep before sunset to enjoy the golden light over the Gulf of Thailand.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat transfer to Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay) — a pristine, undeveloped island just 4.5 km off Kep's coast. White sand beaches, crystal-clear turquoise waters, and swaying palm trees in a completely unspoiled setting. Enjoy a private beach setup — sun loungers, umbrellas, snorkeling equipment, and a dedicated butler service.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling in the coral reefs around Rabbit Island, followed by a kayaking excursion along the island's coastline. Return to the mainland by mid-afternoon. Visit the Kampot Pepper Plantation — a private tour of a premium pepper farm in nearby Kampot, learning about the cultivation of one of the world's most prized spices, with a tasting session and selection of premium pepper products to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a luxury clifftop restaurant in Kep — panoramic Gulf of Thailand views, fresh seafood and Cambodian coastal cuisine. Followed by a private stargazing session on the beach with a local astronomer guide — Kep's low light pollution makes for extraordinary night skies.

meals.breakfast: In-villa or hotel breakfast — tropical fruit, Cambodian omelets, fresh baguettes (French colonial legacy), and coconut coffee
meals.lunch: Private beach picnic on Rabbit Island — gourmet hamper with fresh seafood, salads, tropical fruits, chilled wines, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Clifftop fine dining in Kep — whole grilled lobster, Kampot pepper beef tenderloin, mango sticky rice dessert, with curated wine selection

day_by_day.notes: November weather in Kep is ideal — dry, warm, and sunny with gentle sea breezes. Water visibility for snorkeling is excellent post-monsoon. Apply reef-safe sunscreen. The Kampot Pepper farm visit is a unique luxury experience — purchase aged black, red, and white Kampot pepper as premium gifts.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning in Kep — optional sunrise yoga on the beach or a morning swim. Visit the Kep National Park for a private guided jungle trek — a compact forested hill offering scenic coastal views, butterfly gardens, and rich bird life. The park's trails are well-maintained and suitable for a 2-hour guided walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to Sihanoukville port (approximately 1.5 hours) and luxury speedboat transfer to Song Saa Private Island — Cambodia's most exclusive private island resort in the Koh Rong Archipelago. Check in to an overwater villa or jungle villa. Spend the afternoon on pristine private beaches, swimming in the resort's marine reserve.
day_by_day.evening: Romantic sunset cocktails on the overwater jetty. Private candlelit dinner on the beach — personalized menu created by the resort's executive chef, featuring freshly caught seafood, premium Wagyu beef, and artisan desserts. Under the stars with the sound of gentle waves.

meals.breakfast: In-villa or hotel breakfast in Kep — eggs to order, tropical fruits, pastries, and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at Song Saa Private Island's restaurant upon arrival — light seafood lunch, fresh salads, and chilled tropical cocktails
meals.dinner: Private beach candlelit dinner at Song Saa — bespoke multi-course menu with sommelier-selected wine pairing and personalized dessert

day_by_day.notes: Song Saa Private Island is one of Southeast Asia's finest luxury eco-resorts. The marine reserve surrounding the island is protected — snorkeling and diving reveal extraordinary coral gardens and marine life. Pre-book the private beach dinner as it is a signature experience requiring advance arrangement.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Song Saa Private Island — sunrise snorkeling or diving in the marine reserve with a private dive master. Alternatively, a private sunrise kayak through the mangrove channels. Followed by a luxurious spa treatment at the resort's overwater spa — traditional Khmer massage with organic coconut oil and Kampot pepper body scrub.
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell lunch at Song Saa. Luxury speedboat transfer back to Sihanoukville, then private vehicle transfer to Phnom Penh International Airport (approximately 3.5 hours) or arrange a charter flight for a seamless luxury departure. Final souvenir shopping at the airport's premium boutiques — silk scarves, Kampot pepper, and Cambodian artisan crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Phnom Penh International Airport. Carry with you extraordinary memories of Cambodia's ancient temples, vibrant culture, and pristine coastline.

meals.breakfast: Final island breakfast at Song Saa — tropical smoothie bowls, eggs Benedict with smoked fish, fresh pastries, and specialty coffee on the overwater deck
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Song Saa — signature seafood platter with chilled Champagne, celebrating a magnificent journey
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge dinner depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Ensure all purchases — including Kampot pepper, silk products, and artisan crafts — are properly packed. Cambodia allows export of most artisan goods; antiques require documentation. Allow sufficient transfer time to Phnom Penh airport — 3.5 hours by road from Sihanoukville. A charter flight (45 minutes) is the premium option. Confirm departure logistics with your concierge the evening before.
